title: intent sync --to-store folds a thread's body into its context when it carries a cover edit back, compounding on each carry
body:
Found on 2026-09-24 by vc's subagent auditing `docs/concepts/the-store.md` for the 3.2.1 doc audit, driven in scratch projects on the pair at `4c687eaad`.

Seen: `intent sync --to-store <ID>`, the command that carries a hand edit to a thread's cover back into the store, folds the thread's `body` into its `context`. Driven: `intent set ST0001 body "A body set by the verb"`, `intent st start ST0001`, a hand edit to `## Context`, then `intent sync --to-store ST0001` -- the extract became `"context": "Why: upstream limit.\n\nA body set by the verb"`, and `info.md` then renders the body twice. In a second project the fold compounded to three copies over repeated carries. The renderer writes the body straight after the Context text with no heading of its own (`views.rs:372-387`), and the read-back takes it as part of Context (`ingest.rs:1237-1294`). intentd's ingest carries a changed cover the same way.

Not affected: measured by vc at 2026-09-24 10:17Z by `date -u`, no thread in any estate's store in hv's fleet carries its body inside its context, over every thread with a body; the same query finds the fold in both of the subagent's reproducing stores.

Expected: carrying a cover back never moves text between fields.

Disposition: vc, 2026-09-24 -- one family with 0559, 0556 and 0569; its disposition follows hv's ruling on that family. The docs teach `intent set` for a thread's Objective and Context, which never passes through the read-back.

Corrected forward on 2026-09-24: the fold also happens on the unscoped `intent sync --to-store`, not only the scoped one (vc's working-with-llms subagent, driven with no intentd running).


Fixed in 3.2.2 by `4e4d4cf47` (vc, 2026-09-25): the commit message names the bank, its patch-id and the judge.
